options: Because caching assumes calling a method again safely returns the same result, which isn't true for a method that performs DML
Because cacheable methods cannot return void
Because only getter methods can be @AuraEnabled at all
Because cacheable=true is only valid on trigger handler classes
questions.explain: Cacheable methods are assumed safe to call repeatedly without side effects; a method that writes data via DML breaks that assumption, so it must not be marked cacheable.

questions.q: Per this lesson's rule of thumb, when should you use an imperative Apex call instead of `@wire`?
options: Whenever the method returns a List instead of a single record
Imperative calls should always be preferred over @wire in every situation
When the call should fire as the direct result of a user action, at a moment your own code controls, rather than loading automatically
@wire can only be used in parent components, never in children
questions.explain: The lesson's rule: use @wire when data should load automatically and react to changing inputs; call imperatively when the call is tied to a specific user action you need to control.

questions.q: What mechanism does a child LWC use to notify its parent that something happened, per this lesson?
options: Calling a method directly on the parent component instance
Writing directly to the parent's @track properties
Setting a global JavaScript variable
Dispatching a CustomEvent that the parent listens for in its template
questions.explain: A child cannot call a parent's methods directly in LWC; it dispatches a CustomEvent, and the parent listens for it in its template (e.g. onstatuschange).

questions.q: If a JavaScript file dispatches `new CustomEvent('statusChange', ...)` (camelCase), what does the parent's markup need to listen for?
options: onstatusChange, matching the camelCase exactly
onstatuschange, because Salesforce lowercases custom event names automatically
on-status-change, with hyphens inserted
STATUSCHANGE, in all capitals
questions.explain: Salesforce lowercases custom event names automatically, so a camelCase statusChange dispatch must be listened for as onstatuschange in the parent's markup -- a common source of silent event-handling bugs.

questions.q: Why would this platform need Lightning Message Service instead of a custom event for communication between two unrelated components on the same page?
options: Lightning Message Service is required for all LWC communication, even parent-child
Custom events cannot carry any data in their payload
Custom events only work between components with a direct parent-child relationship; unrelated components need cross-DOM messaging instead
Lightning Message Service is deprecated and should be avoided
questions.explain: Custom events only reach a direct parent listening on the child's markup; components without that parent-child relationship need Lightning Message Service's publish/subscribe model instead.
